newsitem.title: CHINA: China's economic growth just 7.0 pct -- World Bank.
newsitem.headline: China's economic growth just 7.0 pct -- World Bank.

text.p: China's economic growth was just 7.0 percent in the late summer months compared with an official 9.8 percent in the first half, Hong Kong's South China Morning Post on Sunday quoted the World Bank as saying.
China said on Saturday it expected gross domestic product (GDP) to grow by about 10 percent in 1996 and by 10.3 percent in 1997.
China's GDP grew by 10.2 percent in 1995 and Beijing has set an official minimum growth target of eight percent for 1996.

However, the World Bank report quoted by the South China Morning Post said the situation in China's lumbering state sector gave serious cause for alarm. It said about 17 percent of GDP was now created by largely unsellable products of state-owned factories -- more than double the figure quoted by the World Bank last year.
The World Bank report also cited high unemployment, of about 10 percent in urban areas, and even as high as 30 percent in some cities, compared with an official figure of 3.8 percent natonwide.
